figure.purpose: Every amount, quantity, time and count. Tabular numerals are mandatory: a total that reflows while typing is untrustworthy.

display.purpose: Page headings inside the action band and the ledger heading. Never larger than 1.75rem.

body.purpose: Prose, table cells and hints. The system sans, deliberately invisible.

label.purpose: Field labels and table headers: uppercase, tracked 0.1em, so they read as a printed form's captions.

shadows.name: action-lift
shadows.purpose: The band's action button only: a real offset plus a soft blur, so it reads as a physical key.

shadows.name: floating-list
shadows.purpose: The product picker's match list, and nothing else. It floats over content.

shadows.name: record-key
shadows.purpose: The record button's own crimson shadow; it disappears when the button is disabled.

motion.name: stamp-land
motion.purpose: The system's only authored motion. Runs only on the document just recorded, never on a list of documents at once. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: skeleton-sweep
motion.purpose: Loading bars. Bars rather than a spinner, so the header and scope controls do not jump.

narrative.overview:
Tempox is a shop's sales book, and the world is the one a bookkeeper already knows: paper, hairline rules, and ink. The organising idea is that every event wears its state on its face — a sale is a document that has been stamped, not a row carrying a status badge. That is the whole thesis, and it refuses the category default it was built against: the generic admin CRUD where state is a coloured pill nobody reads.

The world lends exactly four things and refuses to lend a fifth: type, palette, density, and one signature move. It never supplies the layout, the navigation model, or the controls. Every control here is the ordinary thing a web application already uses — a text field, a select, a table, a button — because the person behind the counter needs to know where everything is before they notice the world.

Density is high and quiet. This is a working surface seen all day under office light at a fixed PC in a shop, so the ground is paper, not a dark theme chosen because the category likes dark. Expression is spent in one place: the stamp. Everything else is clean, aligned, and deliberately unremarkable, because a screen with one strong idea needs the rest of itself to stay out of the way.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground, hairline rules, ink — no second layer, no texture behind content
One saturated accent (crimson) spent on one action band and the stamp
Condensed humanist for every figure and heading; tabular numerals everywhere
One authored motion: the stamp landing
Standard web controls; the world never re-skins a familiar affordance

rules.name: The One Line System Rule
rules.body: --rule and --rule-strong are the only line values in the system. The sheet's rules and the table's borders consume the same two tokens, because the paper's rules are the table's grid — never a texture painted behind a table. Two line systems would turn the world into a costume.

rules.name: The Crimson Is Spent Rule
rules.body: Crimson appears on the action band, the confirmed stamp, the record button, and the focus ring, and nowhere else. It is never decoration, never a background wash, never a section marker. A page with crimson in three more places has none.

rules.name: The Annulled Is Ink Rule
rules.body: A cancelled document is indigo-black and struck through, never crimson. An annulment is a correction, not an alarm; colouring it crimson would make a cancelled sale look like the worst thing on the page and would spend the accent that belongs to the confirmed stamp.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number a user reads or types — money, quantities, times, dates, counts — is set in the figure face with tabular numerals. No exceptions, including inside inputs.

rules.name: The Label Is Uppercase Rule
rules.body: A field label is uppercase and tracked, and therefore its accessible name is compared case-insensitively; a test that demands one case is asserting the stylesheet, not the design.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Nothing in this system carries a decorative shadow; the three documented shadows are the complete vocabulary, and each one encodes a physical relationship (a key, a floating sheet, a pressed button).

dos: Do set every number in the figure face with tabular numerals.
Do spend crimson on the band, the confirmed stamp, the record button, and the focus ring — and nowhere else.
Do render a g or ml product's unit verbatim: 1,500 g at $0.01/g, never converted to kilograms or litres.
Do strike through an annulled document in ink, and its total with it.
Do show honest empty states that name the next action, and never invent sample rows.
Do keep the single line system: the paper's rules and the table's grid are the same two tokens.
Do wire every shortcut you print on a control.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus) from the palette.
donts: Don't put a texture, gradient, or second rule layer behind content.
Don't use a coloured border-left or border-right above 1px as a card or row accent.
Don't use a hard offset shadow outside the documented vocabulary.
Don't use glyphs or emoji as icons, and don't set the system sans as a display voice.
Don't use gradient text, glass, blur, or a coloured halo for emphasis.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't animate anything but the stamp landing.
Don't let a destination the shop does not sell appear in the rail.
